mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered Agent (licensed under International Companies Act 1988)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consular Legalization of Certified True Copies of Beneficial Owner Passports and Proof of Address

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the Samoa FIU consolidated PEP list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, HM Treasury UK sanctions list, and Samoa's domestic sanctions and asset-freeze notices issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any PEP, family member of a PEP, or close associate, including verification of source of funds and source of wealth. Ongoing transaction monitoring and screening refresh at minimum quarterly and upon any trigger event. Reliance on equivalent jurisdiction due diligence is permitted only for financial institutions in FATF-compliant jurisdictions and under written AML/CFT Act 2018 section 33 arrangements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies and Trusts Office (SICTO) electronic name clearance module via the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Companies Registry portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the operative official language for company names under the Companies Act 2006 and International Companies Act 1988. Chinese-character names are not statutorily recognized in the formal registry; any non-Latin name must be transliterated into a Latin-alphabet English equivalent for registration. The Latin rendering is the sole legal name, with a Chinese-character trading name permitted only if the English legal name is clearly referenced as dominant in the memorandum and articles and on all commercial documentation. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered Samoan company, international company, foreign company registered to carry on business in Samoa, or reserved name. A name must not include any word or expression that in the Registrar's opinion suggests patronage of, or connection with, the Government of Samoa, a foreign government, or any public authority unless prior written consent has been obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Standard name reservations are valid for 30 calendar days from the date the Samoa International Companies and Trusts Office (SICTO) confirms availability. An extension may be requested by written application made to the Registrar of International Companies before the expiry date, supported by a registered agent's cover letter and payment of the extension fee; the Registrar may extend the reservation for up to a further 30 days in the Registrar's discretion. Upon a name rejection, the registered agent must receive the written notice of refusal and may file a new name application without prejudice. If the applicant disputes the refusal, the prescribed procedure is: (1) the registered agent files a notice of appeal in writing with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, including the original name, the statutory ground for refusal, and a memorandum of arguments; (2) the Registrar must consider the appeal and respond in writing within 21 days; (3) if the Registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Samoa for judicial review within 30 days of the affirmation, per the Judicature Ordinance 1961 and applicable civil procedure rules. No oral hearing is granted at the administrative stage unless the Registrar directs otherwise. All appeal costs, filing fees, and registered agent professional fees are borne by the applicant.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the sole registered office for an International Company. The International Companies Act 1988 requires the company to maintain a registered office in Samoa at a physical street address maintained by the licensed registered agent. This address serves as the official service of process location, and cannot be a post office box or virtual co-working desk. The registered agent's physical office address is used for registry filings, statutory records, and receipt of official notices. An operational physical facility for the parcel consolidation hub is not separately mandated for tax status, but for the efficient conduct of the ISIC 5229 cross-border parcel linehaul business the Samoan entity may maintain only a registered-agent address in Samoa and foreign administrative/operations offices abroad. However, the Samoa International Companies regime must not be used for tax evasion; substance requirements are minimal but require at least a registered agent, registered office in Samoa, and maintenance of certain corporate records at the registered office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 2012 (Samoa) — incorporation, memorandum and articles, name restrictions, registered office and registered agent requirements, and tax-exemption provisions; read with the International Companies Regulations (forms and fees); Business Licence Act 1998 and Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 govern any physical presence in Samoa; Companies Act 2001 governs a domestic operating subsidiary if required.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa — applications are submitted exclusively through SIFA-licensed registered agents.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Application for Registration of an International Company, lodged with the Memorandum and Articles of Association; registration is perfected by the Certificate of Incorporation issued under the seal of the International Companies Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; an International Company may fix its authorised share capital in any currency at any amount and need not deposit or escrow any capital at incorporation. Shares may be issued for cash, promissory notes, or other consideration as determined by the directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] adopted in writing by the subscriber-director on [DATE] pursuant to the Articles of Association and the International Companies Act 2012. RESOLVED: (1) that the share subscriptions tendered by the founding subscribers be and are hereby accepted and that shares be allotted and issued, fully paid or credited as paid, and entered in the register of members; (2) that the registered office of the Company be established at the office of its licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and that the registered agent be authorised to act and hold office; (3) that [NAME] be appointed director and [NAME] be appointed secretary with the powers and authorities conferred by the Articles, effective immediately. Approved and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of licensed registered agent and name approval reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed Registered Agent (corporate services provider approved by the Samoa International Finance Authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select and instruct a registered agent licensed by SIFA. The agent submits a name-reservation application to the SIFA International Companies Registry with up to three proposed names in preference order. Each proposed name must end with 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', or 'Société Anonyme' and must not contain a restricted word such as 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Insurance', 'Assurance', or 'Reinsurance' absent a separate licence. The Registry will confirm that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, protected name, or registered trade mark.
required_dossiers: Prescribed name reservation form
Three proposed company names in priority order
AML/CFT due-diligence pack of ultimate beneficial owner(s): certified passport copy, proof of address, bank reference
Registered agent engagement letter
Consent statement of the proposed director(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, the agent may file an alternative name reservation within 5 business days without loss of priority, or apply to the Registrar for a direction that the proposed name be accepted notwithstanding similarity where the existing holder consents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement of incorporation application and memorandum of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — International Companies Registry, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent lodges Form 1 (Application for Registration of an International Company) electronically or at the SIFA Registry counter, together with the signed memorandum and articles of association, subscriber consents, consents of the registered agent and registered office, and the government incorporation fee. The memorandum must state the authorised share capital (no statutory minimum), the class and currency of shares, and the principal purpose: cross-border parcel consolidation and logistics linehaul. The articles may adopt the model form under the International Companies Act 2012 or bespoke provisions. The application is scrutinised for compliance with name, subscriber, and registered agent requirements.
required_dossiers: Form 1 — Application for Registration of an International Company
Memorandum of Association signed by each subscriber
Articles of Association (model or bespoke)
Subscriber consent and witness attestation
Consent of the registered agent
Consent to use of registered office address in Samoa
Declaration of compliance by the registered agent
Receipt of US$100 government filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where a requisition is raised, the registered agent must submit a corrective reply and amended instruments within 14 days; failure to cure leads to deemed withdrawal, and a fresh application with a new fee is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of certificate of incorporation and first board governance actions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — International Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under the seal of the Registry and enters the company in the International Companies Register. The sole subscriber-director then passes the pro-forma first board resolution: accepting share subscriptions and allotting shares, adopting the registered office at the registered agent's address in Apia, and appointing the founding director and secretary. The registered agent prepares the minute, issues share certificates, and opens the statutory registers of members, directors and secretaries, charges, and beneficial ownership.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Signed minutes of the first board resolution
Allotment and share subscription records
Share certificates in prescribed form
Statutory register of members
Statutory register of directors, secretaries and charges
Registered agent acceptance of office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error or omission, apply to the Registrar under the International Companies Act 2012 for rectification supported by a director's certificate; reissue is completed within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax exemption confirmation, business licensing and physical compliance prerequisites
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (Ministry for Revenue); Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the certificate of incorporation and memorandum with the Samoa Revenue Authority to obtain written confirmation of the International Company's tax-exempt status (exempt from income tax on non-Samoan-source income and from exchange control). Because an International Company may not carry on domestic business in Samoa, any physical parcel sorting and linehaul activity within Samoa must be performed through a licensed domestic company or an expressly licensed entity; accordingly, if a facility is established, apply to MCIL for a Business Licence and to PUMA for Development Consent and Building Permit, and obtain fire and occupational clearances. The registered agent files the annual compliance attestation with SIFA.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Tax-exemption confirmation request to Samoa Revenue Authority
MCIL Business Licence application and fee (if domestic physical presence)
PUMA Development Consent and EIA documents (if facility in Samoa)
SFESA fire safety certificate and occupational health clearance
Annual registered agent compliance filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax exemption is queried, provide a written legal opinion confirming the offshore source of all revenue and the IC's non-resident status; if a MCIL or PUMA clearance is refused, restructure the physical hub under a domestic Samoan company (Companies Act 2001) with the applicable licences, or relocate the physical hub to a designated free-zone or export processing zone.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) — Business Licence Division; Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) — Development Consent and Building Permits; Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) — fire safety; Samoa Revenue Authority — revenue clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence (Warehousing, Freight Forwarding and Logistics Support Services) under the Business Licence Act 1998, together with Development Consent and Building Permit under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004; no sectoral postal/courier licence is required for the International Company, which remains a non-resident offshore operator.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration and Preliminary EIA for low-intensity sorting warehouses; Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is directed for facilities exceeding prescribed floor-area thresholds, located in coastal protection zones or water catchments, or handling hazardous or dual-use goods.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Samoa water quality and wastewater discharge standards (no unpermitted discharge; stormwater retention and leachate control), VOC and particulate emissions within workplace and ambient limits, noise levels within environmental nuisance regulations, and licensed solid-waste handling with segregation of e-commerce packaging recyclables and any hazardous rejects.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by SFESA (fire alarm, suppression system, hydrant access and evacuation plan); structural load inspection and certificate of occupancy from PUMA; workplace health and safety clearance under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013, including warehouse racking inspection, manual-handling protocols and emergency response drills; registration with the Samoa Accident Compensation Corporation for employee injury cover.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of the Independent State of Samoa (MOR), National Taxpayer Registration Unit; taxpayer portal: Samoa Online Tax Services (SOTS)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned International Company (IC), the registered agent must file Form IR-01 with the Ministry for Revenue, attaching the certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, registered office confirmation, and AML/CFT due diligence. The Ministry will issue a Tax Identification Number (TIN) upon approval. In practice, an IC wholly conducting offshore business is not subject to income tax and holds a tax exemption certificate issued under the International Companies Act 1987; this certificate is filed with MOR as the governing tax status document. Separate VAGST registration is required only if the IC makes non-exempt taxable supplies in Samoa exceeding the statutory threshold; a non-resident IC may apply for VAGST registration on Form VAGST-REG through its local agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a check-the-box or comparable entity classification election. An International Company is a separate legal person and is conclusively treated as the taxpayer for any Samoan-source activities, but it enjoys a statutory exemption from income tax under the International Companies Act 1987; no hybrid mismatch election is available. A VAGST election to register voluntarily is permitted where the entity supplies taxable goods or services in Samoa, subject to standard rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 200,000 annual taxable turnover measured over any 12-month rolling period
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based clearance, or digital stamping mandate is currently imposed by Samoa. Registered persons must issue compliant fiscal invoices showing the VAGST amount, maintain electronic or physical records prescribed under the Tax Administration Act 2012, and report VAGST on the prescribed periodic return.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Samoa qualify for zero-rating if they are exported within 28 days of the date of supply, the exporter obtains and retains proof of physical export, and the goods leave Samoa for a destination outside Samoa. Services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated when the benefit is provided outside Samoa and the services do not relate to land or tangible goods in Samoa; the consolidation-hub services must be performed for a non-resident counterparty, invoiced in a foreign currency or Tala without VAGST, and supported by written contracts demonstrating offshore delivery.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for direct-injection linehaul
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 foreign-currency receipt evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Comprehensive audit scrutiny applies to all zero-rated export claims. The Ministry for Revenue may assess unrecovered or unsupported VAGST at the standard 15% rate, impose shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 2012 of up to 100% of the tax shortfall for intentional evasion, issue late-payment penalties and interest, and initiate criminal proceedings in respect of knowingly false or fraudulent zero-rating declarations, with fines and imprisonment under the VAGST Act 2007 and Tax Administration Act 2012. There is no limitation period for clawback of refunds obtained by fraud, and principals may be held jointly and severally liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS; Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa) acting as the Exchange Control Authority under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and as bank supervisor under the Financial Institutions Act 1996; the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) oversees AML/CFT reporting under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; the Ministry of Finance grants exchange control exemption orders for offshore entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The WST is not freely convertible on the capital account; current-account WST transactions require authorized-dealer intermediation and CBS documentary reporting, while capital-account WST conversions generally require CBS approval. International Companies (ICs) are statutorily deemed non-resident and non-domestic under the International Companies Act 1987: all IC treasury flows must be denominated in a permitted foreign currency (USD preferred), rendering capital and current account convertibility effectively unrestricted for USD flows with zero CBS/Exchange Control approval thresholds. Profit remittance of IC dividends is freely permitted from audited retained earnings with no Samoan withholding tax, no capital gains tax, and no remittance licensing; only a standing FIU-reportable wire protocol applies for amounts exceeding the USD 10,000 transaction-reporting threshold.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For Samoan resident exporters, Section 3 of the Exchange Control Regulation 1977 requires full surrender of export foreign-currency proceeds to an authorized dealer within 90 days of shipment. ICs are wholly exempt via the Exchange Control (Exemption of International Companies) Notice 1988 because they are non-resident and prohibited from trading with Samoa residents or transacting WST; therefore, USD receivables generated by the parcel-consolidation hub (ISIC 5229 principal in-bound and out-bound linehaul) may be retained offshore or in the IC's USD Samoa account indefinitely with no surrender ratio or conversion timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Offshore International Company USD Operational Account payable in foreign currency only
Offshore IC USD Corporate Account with SWIFT direct-correspondent capabilities and trade-finance desk
Domestic WST Clearing Account for last-mile agent payouts within Samoa; not recommended as primary USD treasury account
Operational Account (retail-oriented; limited offshore IC KYC appetite)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: High, subject to the digital EMI's own jurisdictional risk matrix. Airwallex (operating under Australian or UK EMI/ADL licenses, not under a CBS license) will accept a Samoan IC as the Account Holder if the IC provides a full corporate kit, UBO declaration, and source-of-funds evidence; legal constraint: Samoa has no fintech sandbox and no EMI licensing category, so the EMI is not Samoa-supervised, WST-denominated accounts are unavailable, and all flows must be routed in USD or other supported currencies via the EMI's global clearing network. The IC should hold a BSP or ANZ Samoa USD account as a fallback liquidity buffer because EMIs may freeze accounts pending enhanced CDD when Samoan jurisdictions appear on any EU/FATF watchlist tranche.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoa-licensed banks (BSP and ANZ) generally require a physical or video-verified interview with each bank signatory and with the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) for every corporate account under the CBS Guidance Notes on Customer Due Diligence; a purely remote opening is permitted only where the director completes a banker-attested identity verification at any overseas branch of the same banking group (e.g., BSP Port Moresby or ANZ Sydney) and where the Samoan branch receives the certified KYC pack by tested telex. The Registered Agent (Samoa International Company) must countersign the Account Mandate and issue a Certificate of Incumbency attesting to directors, the incorporator transaction chain, and non-resident status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or opaque ultimate beneficial ownership chain (threshold: 25% equity or control) in the International Company Register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Register of Directors and Shareholders; Beneficial Ownership Declaration signed by the Registered Agent; Certificate of Incumbency dated within 30 days; each UBO's notarized passport, proof of residential address, and bank reference letter from the source-of-wealth jurisdiction; organizational chart evidencing the Samoan IC as top holding vehicle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red flag on non-face-to-face incorporation and absence of commercial substance for a parcel-consolidation hub with no physical Samoa office.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master services agreements with e-commerce platforms and linehaul carriers; forwarder warehouse contracts in Hong Kong/Singapore; third-party logistics (3PL) statements showing the IC's direct injection role; forecast monthly parcel volumes; the IC's audited or internally reviewed financial statements projected for 12 months; CBS-compliant business profile form describing ISIC 5229 activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds ambiguity for initial paid-in capital and any subsequent USD capital injection routed through third-party payment processors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorizing USD capital injection; share subscription agreement; banking statements of the fund-originator account for the trailing 6 months; signed declaration that funds are not derived from gambling, crypto arbitrage, or sanctions-prohibited trade; SWIFT MT103 evidence of direct bank-to-bank remittance avoiding cash or virtual-asset addresses.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Execution standard: SWIFT MT103 (serial payment) from the parent or UBO's bank to the Samoan IC USD account at BSP or ANZ Samoa, with Ordering Customer field matching the shareholder's legal name and Beneficiary field matching the exact IC registration name; remittance information must cite 'ISSUED SHARE CAPITAL / WS_IC / CAPITAL INJECTION' plus the 8-digit IC registration number; the Samoa receiving bank will apply FIU threshold-reporting at USD 10,000 and CBS statistical coding for every inbound credit, so the IC must pre-submit the Certificate of Incumbency and board resolution to the receiving branch before first fund transfer to avoid automatic hold; no exchange control approval certificate is required for ICs because the Exemption Notice 1988 applies; minimum capital is zero under the International Companies Act 1987 but a USD 1,000–50,000 funding level is recommended to demonstrate substance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails hierarchy: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct payments to linehaul carriers, postal operators, and last-mile delivery partners, ensuring dual foreign-exchange (FX) rate quote capture from two authorized dealers before execution; (2) SWIFT MT202 only for bank-to-bank cover after MT103 has been separately transmitted; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) issued by ANZ Samoa or BSP for high-value bulk consolidated shipments to protect against non-delivery of injected parcels; (4) Local Samoa clearing via the Central Bank of Samoa's Interbank Settlement System (RTGS-equivalent) only for WST-denominated last-mile payouts to Samoan agents, with the WST exposure capped below the liquidity reserve; all disbursements above USD 20,000 require board-approved disbursement memos and periodic reconciliation against the 3PL cost dashboard.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/WST vanilla foreign-exchange forwards executed with CBS-licensed authorized dealers (BSP and ANZ Samoa) for haircut hedging of local WST payout legs, standard tenor up to 12 months with no premium payments permitted outside dealer credit lines

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/WST booked offshore with a Singapore or Hong Kong bank counterparty, cash-settled in USD without touching the onshore WST market, used to hedge long-term Samoan agent tariff exposure

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) between USD and WST for any extended WST-denominated warehouse or agent-financing facility, subject to CBS reporting as a non-resident IC derivative transaction and with termination breakage clauses mirroring the IC's fixed 3-year linehaul contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the International Company (incorporation details, registered office, shareholders, directors, and capital confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (FISA) — Registrar of International Companies, via the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) calendar month after the anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of USD 100 per month or part-month for overdue annual return; annual government fee unpaid for six (6) consecutive months triggers Registrar strike-off proceedings, gazetted three (3) months before dissolution with assets vesting in the Public Trustee

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual government license / maintenance fee remittance through registered agent (tiered by authorized capital)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the incorporation anniversary date each year; deemed timely if remitted by registered agent within 30 days of anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 10% of the annual fee after 30 days; continued non-payment beyond six (6) months exposes the company to administrative strike-off, after which restoration requires court order, payment of all arrears (USD 300+), and fresh agent certification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register refresh and annual confirmation (shareholding and controller snapshot)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: FISA, through the licensed registered agent maintaining the Register of Beneficial Owners on-site
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of incorporation; any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the agent within 14 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update beneficial ownership records attracts a fine up to WST 10,000 (approx. USD 3,700) per violation; persistent non-compliance may lead to suspension of the registered agent and administrative strike-off of the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Notification / Return (confirm core income-generating activities and physical presence if the parcel consolidation hub is a 'relevant activity')
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within twelve (12) months following the financial year-end, aligned with the annual return filing cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty up to USD 10,000 for failure to file or for false statements; FISA may escalate to strike-off and notification of home-competent authorities where the company does not satisfy economic substance but claims foreign tax residence

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory independent audit is NOT required for a standard Samoa International Company carrying on qualifying non-licensable activities, provided it is not a bank, insurer, or licensed financial service provider and does not accept public deposits; audit rights may be triggered where shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares request an audit or where FISA issues a direction on public-interest grounds
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Books and records to reflect true financial position; no prescribed GAAP, but international practice accepts IFRS or US GAAP; records commonly maintained in USD with financial statements prepared voluntarily for lending or tax-residence support

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Register of Beneficial Owners must stay at the registered office in Samoa and be updated within 14 days of any share transfer or ownership change; no public UBO filing is required, but the registered agent must attest annually to FISA that the register is complete and current as at the incorporation anniversary, identifying any direct shareholders versus ultimate natural-person controllers of the parcel consolidation hub

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 - 1,500 per annum inclusive of annual return preparation, UBO register maintenance, and government fee handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required for a standard IC; voluntary certified financial statement compilation or audit-ready pack costs USD 1,500 - 4,000 depending on transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% for International Companies: under Section 200 of the International Companies Act 1987, a Samoan International Company (IC) is exempt from all Samoan taxes and duties, including income tax, withholding tax, stamp duty, and estate duty. The exemption is automatic upon incorporation, requires no applying certificate, and is preserved by payment of the annual government fee and compliance with beneficial ownership and economic substance filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IRD-1 — Company Income Tax Return (Samoa Ministry of Revenue eServices portal; paper filing by prior approval only)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the company's accounting year (standard 31 December year-end: return due 31 March; the Commissioner of Inland Revenue may grant a written extension). Not applicable to International Companies, which are statutorily exempt from income tax and from this filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, tax ID (IRD) number, accounting period, registered office and agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: International Companies must NOT submit Form IRD-1. If a foreign accountant requires a nil filing, insert 'Exempt IC — International Companies Act 1987, s.200' in the remarks field and attach the SIFA certificate of good standing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income from Samoan and worldwide sources, excluding amounts exempted by statute.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero for an exempt IC. Do not consolidate IC receipts with revenue of a taxable domestic subsidiary or branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses incurred in producing assessable income; add back non-deductible items such as fines, penalties, and entertainment expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero for an exempt IC. A taxable resident entity operating a hub must allocate parcel sorting, warehousing, and linehaul costs in a separate supporting schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 — Taxable income and tax at 27%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed chargeable income multiplied by the 27% corporate rate, reduced by foreign tax credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Zero for an exempt IC. Resident companies must attach the tax computation and any incentive approval certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 — Tax payable or refund claim
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance due or refundable after applying instalment and imputation credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Zero balance for an exempt IC. Refund claims are remitted only to a Samoan bank account and are subject to Financial Intelligence Unit screening.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty up to SAT 5,000, a late payment surcharge of 2% per month on unpaid tax (accumulating up to 24 months), and civil shortfall penalties up to 150% of the evaded amount. Fraudulent evasion attracts criminal fines and imprisonment up to 7 years.
